messages:
Sara: quick spike from a customer using our Go sample app for bulk exports. they followed the quickstart which enables prefetch by default and hit quota/latency pain.

Dennis: what happened exactly?

Sara: their exporter does streaming fan-out: for each page we spawn workers to transform then ship to downstream. with prefetch=3 and maxConcurrency=12 we see sudden bursts to upstream when the workers finish, plus many retries during transient 429s. the client then re-prefetches and we get a cyclical surge.

Yuki: Go SDK defaults prefetch=3? I thought we standardized to 1 across SDKs.

Sara: onboarding quickstart for Go still shows prefetch=3 in the sample snippet. new users copy-paste and get surprising behavior.

Tom: logs?

Sara: excerpt:

```
[08:11:01] prefetch started p=1..3
[08:11:05] workers busy=0 -> drain -> send-burst 50 reqs/200ms
[08:11:05] upstream 429 x18
[08:11:06] retries spawned -> prefetch kicks more pages
[08:11:07] observed cost spike + latency SLO breach
```

Dennis: aha. two problems: (1) sample app encourages aggressive prefetch, (2) backpressure is not propagated through the worker pipeline so prefetching doesn't wait for downstream bottlenecks.

Yuki: parity note: node and py quickstarts were updated to prefetch=1 earlier this year. looks like Go docs missed the change. let's fix docs ASAP.

Tom: engineering fixes?

Sara: idea: add a "prefetchGrace" option that waits until auth/token stability and worker queue depth < threshold before starting prefetch. plus: make prefetch default=1 in Go and add backpressure hooks to the paginator so it `await` enqueues when downstream buffer is full.

Dennis: prefer a simpler immediate fix: change quickstart to prefetch=1 and add a prominent note about pipelines + retry interactions. longer term, add the prefetchGrace and a `pauseOnBackpressure` flag that pauses prefetch when downstream channel depth > 75%.

Yuki: also add a small sample in onboarding showing "safe bulk export": call `await client.auth.EnsureFresh()` before `paginate`, set `prefetch=1`, and drain with bounded worker pool. that should prevent most user errors.

Tom: tests: add integration test that simulates slow worker + transient 429 and assert sustained RPS <= maxConcurrency and no bursts. also add telemetry metric `sdk.prefetch.pause_count` and alert when pause_count > 0 in many customers.

Sara: created issue and repro: #1866. CI job link: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/1866-go-prefetch-grace-repro. assigning to @yuki for docs patch and @tom for SDK change.

onboard-bot: Issue #1866 created: "Go quickstart prefetch default causes export bursts; add prefetchGrace and backpressure pause".

Yuki: I'll update the quickstart and add a migration note in the release notes. Tom, please coordinate parity tests with node/py.

Tom: will do. thanks for catching this — surprised it slipped through onboarding reviews.

Sara: ping me when PRs land; I'll update the customer and recommend immediate workaround (prefetch=0 or call EnsureFresh + bounded workers). :thumbsup:
